items.title: David Weinstein Interview, 1988-09-22
items.q: I went to Jackson, Mississippi in 1929 and spent practically a year up there with Harry Barth, who had a little road band there... This was a starvation trip.

ctx.x: In the 30s, you also went off to New York, right?

I? No. No, no, no. I didn't go to New York then at all. Did you? I went to Jackson, Mississippi in 1929 and spent practically a year up there with Harry Barth, who had a little road band there, very unsuccessful. This was a starvation trip. We had a lot of fun. Harry Barth had played bass with Ted Lewis for years, and he was a Mississippi boy, wanted to come home and start his own band, and it didn't work out, you know. When did you first go to New York? Oh, I didn't get to New York. I've never been to New York…
been a great regret. You had something to do with the recording sessions that Sharkey did in New York
